newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli politicians want top-secret facility moved.
newsitem.headline: Israeli politicians want top-secret facility moved.

text.p: An Israeli legislator and a mayor took aim on Tuesday at a top-secret institute near Tel Aviv that foreign news reports have said works on biological and chemical weapons.

"Life and death cannot be held hostage to one broken test tube," Labour lawmaker Rafi Elul was quoted as saying in a statement to a special parliamentary committee discussing the present location of the biological institute in Nes Ziona.
Israel has declined comment over the years on news reports in France and elsewhere that the facility, in a commuter suburb of Tel Aviv, was working on biological and chemical weapons.

"During time of war the area is a strategic target for the enemy and it would be worthwhile to check if its location does not endanger the entire city," Nes Ziona Mayor Yossi Shvo told the committee on Tuesday.
Shvo told Reuters on Monday he wanted the institute kicked out of town after revived reports in France of arms production three years ago.

Labour lawmaker Dahlia Itzhik said at Tuesday's meeting: "It is fitting to say that there is nothing to justify hysteria but it is even more fitting that a professional committee check the issue before a catastrophe occurs and not afterward."
Experts assured committee members the institute was safe and was run according to the highest international standards as it had for the past 45 years.
"There is nothing in the institute's operations that endangers the environment," institute manager Dr Avigdor Sheferman said.
Elul said a joint committee would be established with the parliamentary foreign affairs and defence committee to review the plant's impact on the environment.
The plant, hidden behind high walls in an industrial area, has long been shrouded in secrecy.

The former deputy head of the Nes Ziona plant, now 79-year-old Marcus Klingberg, was sentenced to 20 years in jail in 1983 for spying for the former Soviet Union. Censors banned news of the affair until a decade after he was jailed.
On Tuesday a parole board turned down Klingberg's request that he be freed due to poor health, a police spokeswoman said.
Klingberg told Israel Radio when asked how he felt being denied release: "Disappointment...They've issued a death sentence and that's that".
